laws.rule: The legal age for cannabis in Nova Scotia is 19. Adults may carry up to 30 g of dried cannabis (or equivalent) in public, and buy only from government-operated stores.

Cannabis Control Act, S.N.S. 2018, c. 3: nobody may buy cannabis except from an authorised cannabis seller (s. 20(2)); a young person (under 19) may not possess, consume, buy or try to buy it (s. 16); nobody may consume cannabis, medical-use cannabis included, in a vehicle except in circumstances set by regulation (s. 22); cannabis carried in a vehicle must be in closed or fastened-closed packaging and out of reach, or not readily accessible, to everyone in the vehicle (s. 23).

Smoke-free Places Act, S.N.S. 2002, c. 12: 'smoke' includes lit or heated cannabis and e-cigarettes, so these bans cover cannabis too. Smoking is banned in school grounds (s. 5(2)), on patios (s. 5(3)), in a motor vehicle with anyone under 19 in it, with windows open or not (s. 5(2A)), and within 4 metres of a building air intake, open window or entrance to a workplace (s. 5(4)). Section 5A bans smoking in provincial parks, on beaches, within 20 metres of playground equipment or sports areas, and on trails or within 9 metres of them. Exceptions: occupied campsites and areas designated for smoking inside provincial parks (s. 5A(2)); private residence land and, outside provincial parks, occupied campsites (s. 5A(3)).

The legal drinking age in Nova Scotia is 19: liquor may not be sold, supplied or given to anyone under 19 except for medicinal purposes (Liquor Control Act, R.S.N.S. 1989, c. 260, s. 89). Being intoxicated in a public place is an offence (s. 87).

Nobody may drive or have care or control of a motor vehicle or off-highway vehicle, moving or not, while in possession of liquor or with liquor in the vehicle, unless it is in an unopened container, in the trunk or another place not readily accessible, behind the rearmost seat of a wagon, van, SUV or hatchback, or in a pickup's exterior compartment or storage space, in a baggage compartment on a motorcycle or off-highway vehicle, or kept out of the driver's reach in a recreational vehicle (Liquor Control Act, s. 54(6)). Opening or drinking liquor in or on a motor vehicle is banned except in an RV parked as a temporary residence on camping or RV land (s. 54(7)).

Art Gallery of Nova Scotia, Halifax: Do not touch artworks or consume food/drinks in exhibition spaces. Large bags, backpacks, umbrellas and pens are excluded from those spaces; the guide offers a coatroom and lockers. Service dogs are permitted.

Art Gallery of Nova Scotia, Halifax: Personal photography is allowed unless otherwise noted, with flash off to protect artworks. This guide does not establish commercial, community or storytelling permission.

items.text: You must be 19 or older to use, buy, grow or possess cannabis. Adults may carry up to 30 g of dried cannabis (or equivalent) in public, and buy only from the Nova Scotia Liquor Corporation (NSLC), in its stores or online. Cannabis in any form can't be used in a vehicle, by the driver or passengers. Using combustible cannabis in a public place where it's banned can bring a fine of up to C$2,000 (about A$2,033, at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026, A$1 = CAD 0.9838).

The Smoke-free Places Act covers smoking and vaping cannabis as well as tobacco: not on or within 20 m of playgrounds in outdoor public spaces, on or within 9 m of public trails, in provincial parks or on provincial beaches (except inside a rented campsite), on licensed patios, or in a private vehicle with anyone under 19 in it. Municipalities can add their own limits.

From 25 June 2026 fines rose: buying cannabis anywhere other than the NSLC is C$600 to C$5,000 (about A$610 to A$5,082), and a person under 19 found with cannabis faces C$250 to C$500 (about A$254 to A$508).

The legal drinking age is 19; the ticket schedule lists drinking by a person under 19 as its own offence (C$295, about A$300). Being intoxicated in a public place is an offence with a C$134 ticket (about A$136, at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026, A$1 = CAD 0.9838).
